attempts.summary: Deployed a sandboxed systemd service named inventory-worker on node1 via an Ansible playbook (localhost/local connection). The service runs as a dedicated 'inventory' system user, writes heartbeats only to /var/lib/inventory (owned 0750 by that user), and is hardened with NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome, PrivateTmp/Devices, capability stripping, etc., with ReadWritePaths limited to /var/lib/inventory. Verified the service is active/enabled and confined (writes inside the directory succeed; writes to /etc fail read-only under the identical sandbox profile). Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol on both node1 and node2: captured pre-restart boot markers (uptime -s, boot_id) and health, triggered a native reboot on one node at a time via a detached nohup+reboot so the ack returned first, polled until each node was reachable again, and confirmed a new boot_id/boot time plus recovered required services (inventory-worker auto-restarted with a new PID on node1, its log continuity proves /var/lib/inventory data persisted across reboot; node2's core services returned active).
